messages:
Maya Tran: taking handoff, I'm primary for the next 6h (til 20:00 UTC). quick heads-up: saw elevated tail latency on prod-gen last 30m, seems correlated with kv-cache misses and an increase in small seq requests. i collected the slowest traces in S3.

incident-bot: Pager triggered: gen-service-high-latency (P3) - 1778889700. symptoms: 95th pct latency up from 240ms -> 1.2s; error rate steady. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1778889700

Alan Chen: thanks. are we seeing CPU/GPU hotspots or just cache churn? do we need to promote secondary?  

Maya Tran: current metrics: CPU and GPUs look fine. Redis cluster shows rising key evictions on shard-2 and increased network RTT between gen-pool-a and redis-2. suspect network flaps -> kv cache thrash. fallback behavior should hit model cold-starts which explains tail latency.

Sophia Gupta: pinging ops to check network path. runbook notes below — quick pointers:
- check redis evictions: `redis-cli -h redis-2 INFO stats | grep evicted`
- confirm kv cache hitrate: dashboard -> GenService / KVCache -> hit_rate
- if shard is flapping, set routing override to avoid redis-2: `redwood routing set --service gen-service --avoid redis-2`
- if sustained, trigger KV cache fallback to local LRU: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-fallback --service gen-service --local-cache-size 8GB`

Maya Tran: adding the minimal incident play: 1) avoid the bad shard 2) warm local cache 3) watch 95th -> if no improvement, fallback to smaller batch sizes to reduce tail.

incident-bot: Suggested runbooks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback , https://redwood.internal/runbooks/redis-eviction-triage

Alan Chen: can you post the commands for the routing override + who can approve? I can push the override if Maya ok.

Maya Tran: go ahead Alan. approver is me — i'll ack and monitor. command (internal):
```
redwoodctl route update --service gen-service --policy avoid:redis-2 --priority 100
```

Sophia Gupta: ops update: network team confirmed transient flaps between datacenter-A rack-7 and redis-2, they've moved redis-2 traffic to interconnect-b. still seeing some packet loss drops. they recommend routing override + restart of gen-worker pods to re-establish healthy prefix caches.

Maya Tran: doing a rolling restart of gen-pool-a workers but with slow drain to avoid client impact. command:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/gen-worker -n prod --grace-period=60
```

Alan Chen: after override + restart, i'll snapshot cache hitrate and latency. if 95th stays >800ms after 15m, we trigger local kv fallback and reduce batch size:
```
redwoodctl scale --service gen-service --batch-size 1
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-fallback --enable
```

Sophia Gupta: added quick checklist to thread:
- [x] route override applied by Alan
- [x] gen-worker restart started by Maya
- [ ] observe 15m window for 95th latency
- [ ] enable local fallback (if needed)
- [ ] notify CS if >30m degraded (so they can update customers)

Maya Tran: route override done (Alan), restart in progress. monitoring: https://redwood.internal/dash/gen-service?range=30m. ping me if any alert spikes.

Alan Chen: confirmed override & routing rules: `avoid:redis-2` active. seeing hitrate up 12% after 4m. 95th down to ~580ms (from 1.2s). nice.

incident-bot: Note: automatic canary rollback disabled for this service during incident. commands executed logged to /var/log/incidents/1778888888.log

Sophia Gupta: if latency keeps improving we can keep this as mitigation and schedule redis-2 maintenance. runbook pointer for post-incident: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/postmortem-template

Maya Tran: sounds good. i'll stay on primary until 20:00 UTC and hand off to @Sophia if stable. quick handoff note for next oncall: avoid changing model variants during recovery, don't flip to lower-quant models unless asked — it hides the real failure mode.

Alan Chen: noted. will update pager duty with mitigation steps and add ops ticket to follow up with network team.

Maya Tran: wrapping up: current status: partial mitigation in place, 95th improved to 460-580ms, no error rate change, continuing to monitor. if we see evictions spike again, escalate to infra and enable local kv fallback. :thumbsup:

Sophia Gupta: i'll take primary if Maya signs off at handoff time. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
